reviews.review:
So I wrote a review a while back on this game and decided to delete it. Because its no longer valid.

I've tried several times to return to this game, what attracted me in the first place to play this game, well there's better games for that now. So i ask, what does this game have to offer? Well, nothing special.

Enemy, level, and Gunplay Mechanics, they absolute get repetitive. Shoot vampire till it enters stake state, stake it, done. What about UV Guns? Just point till they turn to stone.

There's no moment that really jumps out to me in 27 hours of gameplay with the story. I usually give games a lot of leniency when it comes to story. But 27hrs and I can't think of more than one story moment that stood out to me?

In the end, get on sale. Not worth the 70 dollars! Was a buggy mess at launch that kept me from being able to push through and continue playing by the time they patched it. Might try again when they release DLC character since I can't get a refund on this one.

reviews.review: I got the Bite Back addition, you can't really make it without it because it comes with 4 characters with supernatural powers or advantages that give you that edge you need, and it comes with a stake that you need to kill the first vampire (you don't get a stake until AFTER this encounter). You can't kill a Vampire without a stake and so you will fail until you buy the Bite Back Upgrade. Redfall was ninty-nine dollars. After playing the first mission can I say this game is worth the ninty-nine dollars? No it is not. I have games that I have paid less than thirty dollars (GTA5) that have much better graphics and game mechanics. Would I buy Redfall again; had I known and have the experience of playing? Yes, I would buy it again, I like it; it is unique and there is not another Vampire game that I have liked at all. I was wanting a vampire game that I want to keep playing and Redfall is it. I'm sure improvements will come with future updates. Cheers!

Worst game I have ever bought. Steam would not even bother refunding it to me. The only reason I bought this game was to play with my friends and they can't even run the game properly. Waste of money.
if you have friends that will play with you, otherwise the game is stacked against a solo player.

I do not understand the intense hate this game is getting. If you had game-breaking bugs, that's one thing. I personally have only experienced a handful of minor bugs in 25 hours of play, but I completely understand being dissatisfied with a game that doesn't work. I've been playing exclusively multiplayer and it's fun! Not amazing (definitely a lot of features I wish they added like crafting, weapon customization, more things to spend currency on, and more diverse enemies) but nowhere close to the dumpster fire other people keep saying it is. It's an Arkane game! It looks and feels and plays like an Arkane game! I dig it. I don't know...
This was free with my Video card. I would have much rather had a cheaper video card... I feel like I paid too much....
Seriously?? Completely unfinished trash. Why even release it.
I cant recommend this game in it's current state. It feels very unfinished. The world is empty and the AI interactions are laughable at times.

Edited - I freaking hate this game. It was fun in co-op with my husband, then we both got ticked because it was the same thing every time. The same quests, but in different locations with a different boss. 

We all got duped by this studio. We played on the hardest setting and NOTHING really changed. There is no real exploring, no true story, and it's lame. 

Bethesda should be sad to have its name attached to this game.  I have over 500 hours invested in Skyrim, and Fallout 4. I love that both of those games are huge, with many interactions, and the ability to mod them to create even more quests. I miss the character creation, exciting battles, and exploration. I had hoped that the "nest" quests in Redfall would add some of that excitement, but it becomes as mundane as the constant chaos levels in Tiny Tina's Wonderlands (but TTW was a lot more fun). 

I had hoped that the creators of this game would say something.. offer something, and improve everything, but it has been a big nothing. It's all pretty sad.


***The thumbs down is because unless a person buys this on sale, it really isn't worth it until the company fixes it.
Worst game I’ve played to date, I walked for a straight hour without any interactions, dull and boring 24/7, only good thing about it is the unique and beautiful scenery, gameplay is horrifying.

[h2]YES...[/h2]
- It's a good shooter
- Interesting open-world exploration or sight-seeing
- Stealth and Action possiblity with AI adatpting to it
- Idea is somewhat new and unexplored
- 4 playable character with distinct combat/stealth mechanics
- A full skilltree with manifold skills
- A loot system with alot of items laying around, making the world "lived-in"
- A rarity system that adds boni on you weapons
- A level system that make your old weapons obsolete and keep you searching for better
- A variety of weapon types to choose from and to customize your playstyle

[h2]BUT...[/h2]
- Horrible shooting animations, lagging reloads (rubberbanding magazines lagging behind the animations)
- They made so much effort to be interesting and diversified but then just plain copy-pastat all the rest of the assets. "Dungeons" (Hearts) are only just not enough variety to stay interesting
- The Human-AI is not optimized for neither stealth or shooting and they switch between those two modes it jarring and results in T-Posing, gliding around, rubberbanding, deforming (e.g. holding their weapon behind their back to shoot at you and more)
- Vampires is not your everyday concept for horror, but could be soooo good if they wouldn't have littered the whole world with them and made them extreme push-overs 
- Don't bother about every one of the characters, one has UV powers and teleport. Every other it focused on the humans that are already easy as all heck. Please make at least TWO usefull against the 2 types of enemies...
- Every skill needs to be skilled in order to get in the upper skilltree, rendering the possibility to decide obsolete
- No item is used in any meaningful way, the give you health by chugging any drinkable, eatable (may it be chips to full on bottles full with alcohol) and the other give you "support" what is essential just a unfitting word for mula, money, kaching-kaching. You EVEN SPEND IT. Where on earth you spend "support" on weapons. Make it money ffs.
- The "rarity" system is completely obsolete, because every unique weapon is not at all unique and you find them at specific points after a short wait of a in-game day or smth like that
- You always need the new weapon, because the enemies scale with your level so even your best weapon ts bad fast. Not like other games where a "normal" weapon is worth a level or two and unique weapons worth five or more. It feels immediately outdated and you need to skavenge more robbing you essentially of gametime that could be spend playing the story and having fun
- 2 weapon variations for every type of weapon for a looter shooter is just not enough and boring as HECK

[h2]AND...[/h2]
It's sadly the principle of "death by thousand cuts". 

Map Problems:
- Small bugs in Models, 
- off-limit housing in an exploration game,
- to little loot in a looter shooter,
- HOLLOW-MAN VOICE LINE SPAM,
- detection through solid objects,
- Hitscan in a 2023 game,
- Damage range dropoff (like I play a game of nerf against aimbots with nailguns)
- Enemies plain missing / not spawning in

Coop Problems:
- Coop Partner interaction voice line spam (all two of them),
- Coop Hit-box Wandering,
- Coop animations are bugged,
- So.much.missing.collision

No eye for detail:
- floating world-objects
- models clipping through walls,
- low-res textures,
- bugging/skipping/vibrating/missing assets all over the game

Poory optimized rendering pipelines
- textures blurry,
- laggy on mid-to-high settings on a high-end-pc,
- framedrops of doom,
- stutters
- and crashes

I want to like it, but it drained every drop of fun out of the experience for me. That's the only "Vampire"-Mechanic they nailed. It's dry as bones, sucked empty by the lack of creativity, attention to detail and plain "don't care" attitude by the devs/publisher to the obvious flaws this game has.

I honestly feel like everyone is being too harsh on this game.

I'm not going to say it's amazing. And it DEFINITELY isn't up to the standards of Deathloop, Dishonored 2, or (my favorite Arkane game) Prey. Not even close. And I won't pretend that I'm not disappointed about that. I am. I went into this hoping for basically a Borderlands game but with the quality and wonder of the previous Arkane games. And it is NOT that.

But at the same time, people calling it the "worst game of the year" and "not even worth playing for free on game pass" are being hyperbolic and cruel. It's not THAT bad. I don't find the game world to be empty like other people are saying. Especially once (slight spoiler) vampire nests and the Rook Storm are introduced. I find the gun play satisfying enough, I enjoy the character abilities a lot, and the story is nice! I've beaten the game as Devinder, I've started the game as Jacob & Layla to try them out, and I'm currently playing multiplayer as Remi. And I'm still enjoying it a lot. Enough that I still plan to play through the game again (at least a little) as the extra characters they plan to release later.

The ONLY actual problem I have is the difficulty scaling in multiplayer. The game can sometimes be challenging solo, but in multiplayer, it is so easy it's boring (unless you have already beaten the game once and set it to the highest "Eclipse" difficulty). The game needs to either SIGNIFICANTLY beef up the enemies in multiplayer or make the hordes much much larger.

But every other complaint I've seen people mention? I'm not saying they aren't legit, but I don't think they're as bad as people are pretending they are. Although, to be fair, I don't really care about graphical glitches. I find it silly when people act like that sort of thing ruins a game. But if graphical issues are SUPER important to you, that will definitely be a problem.

Overall I would say that the game is good but not great in solo...and okay in multiplayer. It's definitely not as terrible as some people like to say, but not as good as I was hoping it would be. And the few legit issues it does have seem like things that could get patched.

Feels like a parody of a triple-A game made by a parody of a studio released by a parody of a publisher that is owned by Microsoft who feel like a parody in themselves when it comes to gaming.

As many others mentioned before, Redfall plays like a 20€ - 30€ early access game created by an indie developer who hasn't really figured out yet what sort of generic game they want to make.

It tries to be a shooter, but the mechanics are basically worse than those of many games from 10 - 15 years ago.
It tries to be a story driven adventure, but lacks both an interesting story and any engaging storytelling outside constant voice-overs and a lot of dull flashbacks.
It tries to be an open-world game, but the world itself feels surprisingly static, without much sense of wonder and barely any reason for exploration beyond the main story missions.
It tries to be a stealth game during many missions, but once you bring a couple of friends with you pretty much everything can be and will be steamrolled.
It tries to be a multi-player game, or it was at least marketed as one, but it even lacks basic features one would expect from an always online single-player game.
[b]However, worst of all:[/b] It tries to be a game about Vampires, but neither re-invents their interactions or depiction nor conforms to the long established norms of the genre.

If one looks a bit closer at some of the mechanics and past the bugs, glitches or quirks, one has to wonder if the studio could have made a decent game with another year or two of development time or if we finally have entered the era of gaming where people happily pay for perceived quantity of content over any resemblance of quality of that content in video games.
Maybe MS goes for a "No Man's Sky"-style rework of this game, but personally I'd guess some game devs in Austin will be looking for a new studio soon.

At least Redfail has also some funny moments... finding PlayStations placed in the game world fits this lackluster XBox exclusive very well.

Oof. I am a huge fan of Arkane games and I was very excited for this game. The biggest thing is that this game was marketed as a co-op experience, but there is no public matchmaking. This is a huge mistake, considering that all 4 characters seem to require other teammates to really shine. This, combined with terrible and untested AI and the mostly empty open world that feels like a chore to walk through, it’s definitely not worth any amount of money. It’s fun for a bit, but every fight has the same loop, and the bugs don’t help. It would be nice if studios actually launched their games on any system before collecting the audience’s money. This is a scam, at best.
Worst game I've played in over 10 years, BF2042 is about 10x's better.
Terrible. Seriously just pass on this game. Under any circumstance or excuse you give yourself

Disappointing release from Arkane. It is an ok game if it had been release by a relatively unknown developer, but this is Arkane with Microsoft behind it and this is the output? Massive disappointment. Go play Prey, Dishonored, or even Borderlands instead.

Not as horrible as some have said.  For me, video optimization and such are things that can be patched, but game SYSTEMS can't really be changed after launch.  And the weapon system just...doesn't work.  The random spawning of weapons just creates a boring tedious system of having to unequip old version and requip new version of the same weapons.  It would have made more sense to have a sytstem to upgrade the weapons a la Dishonored upgrade system at the Black Markets.

But ultimately what killed the game for me is that it is NOT fun for single player.  The powers of the characters are clearly meant to be for co-op.  And the story isn't as rich if you don't play co-op (and have the characters befriend and talk to each other).  I love Arkane games because I love great single player, story driven game with cool powers and excellent level design.  This has the elements of all of it, but it was clearly designed for co-op as its primary focus.

In the final analysis, the video issues and bugs probably would have been overlooked if the gameplay was actually fun.  Alas, it is not.

Needs work, but there's definitely a good game in there- I'd give it a few months unless you're like me and don't mind working around bugs. 

Writing is on-point, making Peter Thiel and his acolytes into literal vampires that you can kill is a pretty fun concept. I enjoyed Remi as the single-player protagonist, and the major NPCs were mostly likeable characters with some interesting stuff to say over the course of the game.

The combat could use some polish but generally felt good, all the weapon classes felt like they had unique strengths and weaknesses and the special vampires had neat gimmicks. As a looter-shooter it has fairly simple but generally well-balanced perks, and what seem to be a fair number of different weapon parts a la Borderlands; sights and suppressors definitely matter, the others may just be cosmetic. I found myself using blue and purple weapons over yellows frequently, the M1911 with silver bullets is the only one that really stood out to me as busted.

Give it a shot now if you liked Prey/Dishonored and don't mind bugs, otherwise I'd give this one a couple months to work out some kinks.

NB! I would really recommend waiting for a discount, scrolling through the comments i feel like the price is REALLY hurting this game and i have to agree with that, 
placing this game among other AAA+ games is really not very realistic and it is sure to piss a lot of people off making them feel lied to.

I've only payed a few hours into the game so far with 3 other friends.
In short, I do agree that the price is way to high for a game of this ''standard'' but i AM actually enjoying my experience with it so far.

i do NOT feel like i want to play a solo run of the game just yet, it is indeed intended for multiplayer, so if you are looking for something to play alone then there are far better options out there, but if you want to kill some vamps , score some loot and have a decent time with some friends then have at it. 
just turn your expectations to low and expect the unexpected.
NB! I would really recommend waiting for a discount.

it starts slow but the stronger you get, the stronger the vamps get.  Some of the bigger fights with more vamps are intense and fun.  I agree with others that the AI needs to be punched up in its awareness factor to not seem so stupid, however the longer I play the more fun I'm having.

Redfall is a comfy 6/10 game. If you know what I mean, you know what I mean.

Its definitely not going to win any awards for pushing boundaries or for doing anything new or fresh but its a fun game that is worth a play-through. Maybe not for £59.99 though.

I played through the game as Jacob and while I excepted him to be a brooding edgelord he actually ended up having some fairly touching monologues and dialogue with other characters that actually made his character grow on me over the course of the game.

Honestly its a shame the game has had such a harsh reception. The game has its issues for sure and could've absolutely used more time in the oven to iron out bugs and performance issues but its definitely not the horrific mess people are making it out to be, I've definitely played much much worse games.
Sorry, tried to like it, but uninstalled and unless they do some serious improvements am unlikely to was my time with piece of tripe again.

game runs horribly, it's flawed, it's janky. it needed more time in the oven. but i don't know. my friend and i are having an absolute blast, loving the designs and odd plot points, and there's charm to the characters that ARE fleshed out. hopefully things improve in the future, but for now it's a neat little mess of a thing.

I, for one, really love this game. I know a lot of people have had performance issues, but I expect those to be ironed out. If you somehow have a smooth experience or are willing to wait for the patches, you'll look at a beautiful game, with fresh mechanics and an interesting story. 
	I've played through half of it on Gaming Pass and then I loved it enough to buy it on Steam, and playing again the first half, I enjoyed as much as the first time. The combat is challenging and I haven't had any encounters with non-reactive enemies so far. Being able to blast through 3 vampires or more at once is really rewarding. I love the level design, and it's clear to me that a lot of love has been put into designing the game, despite all the negative reactions. Maybe time will tell. 
	The dungeons could use a little more variation, though. They're optional, but they're a nice change of pace and scenery, so I wouldn't mind a few new levels there. Cheers!

I was really looking forward to Redfall. Story driven open world looter shooter with vampires? Sign me up. I even paid full price for it. Unfortunately Redfall just...man, it sucks.

It's not story driven - there seems to be a story here amidst all the notes and recordings but it lacks depth. There's an open world, but it's empty. I frequently run for several minutes across the world and encounter no enemies at all and nothing interesting to investigate. There's loot, but even though it uses a coloured rarity system the level is really all that matters. The shooting is awkward. There are only a few types of vampires and they also share very few models. 

The game itself is buggy. Controls randomly stop working, menu elements get stuck on screen. You can't pause when playing singleplayer. I really wanted to like Redfall, but it's such a chore to play that I'm not going to continue.

I do think it could be made good, but the game would need to be overhauled rather than just bugfixed. 4/10.

A lot of ink's been spilled over this game already, so I'm going to write about a couple specific reasons why I don't recommend it, at least at its $70 face value. Before diving in, I want to say the graphical issues haven't really bothered me. The art style is very Arkane, and if you like the look of the DIshonored games, you'll like the look of this one.

First and foremost, this game is most like Borderlands, but unlike Borderlands, lacks for variety in its gameplay. Go to a slightly different area of town, shoot the same 10 bad guy models, of which there are 3 variations (SMG guy, shotgun guy, sniper guy), hope for loot. Instead of weaponry exploding everywhere, maybe a bag with some loot in it drops.

Which leads to the second big issue with variety. If it's going to be a co-op loot shooter, the loot and gun play needs to feel great. The UV gun is hilariously fun against vampires, but overall there's a maybe 15-weapon pool, and not a lot of diversity in that pool. However, that's not the most infuriating aspect. That award goes to silencers, which actually work and give you stealth, but there's no way to tell if a gun has one unless you equip the weapon, and you can't add them on later! Not to mention shooting just doesn't feel very tight. You'll line up a headshot with a sniper rifle (with no stabilize button, btw. Come on, it's 2023, and my character is THE SNIPER GUY), and it'll whiff by a foot. You can't tell if it's you, the game, or both.

I have primarily been playing this game in co-op with a friend on Gamepass. The multiplayer is...decent, if I'm being generous? The game certainly feels better with friends, but is hamstrung by bugs, missions hard-locking if your friend takes some actions, etc. Even more annoyingly, there's no drop-in, drop-out element. If your friend DC's, your session terminates and you're back to main menu. Friends can't join on you either--they have to be invited to your session.

What's most upsetting though is that this is a game I actually wanted to like, and just...struggle to find positive things to say about. If my buddy isn't available, it just lives in my library gathering dust. It feels like even after the long delay, this game still walked out the front door feeling unpolished.

Redfall, very clearly, has been received poorly, however I don't believe the game is as bad as most are describing.  You have the obligatory performance issues on random rigs, some AI Jank that can easily be patched, the normal kinds of bugs that you find in an open world like this which can also be patched, etc.  Nothing I would consider game breaking or detrimental to the game, its no Cyberpunk or Darktide release.

The storyline seems meh so far and the world does seem empty..especially in this day and age where we're so used to open world games having literally 20 things to do around each corner.  Maybe this is a good thing, maybe it's not...that's yet to be seen by me. The graphics seem nice, though I think the flashligh is a bit flat and lack luster.  The combat unfortunately is mediocre at best, but perhaps that's just the character I'm currently playing I plan on trying others when I find the time (Grown up life, am I right?).  I have, unfortunately, not been able to play with anyone as no one wants to buy the game with the bad press it's getting so I don't have any idea how the multiplayer is.  

I've experienced some bugs, the biggest and most annoying one for me is enemies will just suddenly stop registering damage and I'll have to stop firing and start again for it to start doing damage again.  It's not me missing or anything like that, they just simply stop taking damage and it appears to be random so it's not anything I can easily reproduce from what I've seen.  For the most part my game play has been unbugged and the game runs well on my Ryzen 3950x and 3090 Ti at  5120x1440.  I've not had any noticeable hitching or frame drops, I've not personally noticed any memory leaks or any strangeness when running the game.  

Is this game great...no, by no means.  Is it bad...to some I'm sure it is but honestly it's not as bad as the hate seems to be making it.  It's a pretty bog standard open world looter shooter with what I would consider normal issues for a game of it's type.  Give it a try, if you really hate it then steam has a great refund policy.

Lots of stuttering (RTX 3090ti, i7 13700kf) most uneventful prologue I've played in a recent game and for bonus points..

Despite the fact I was playing on mouse+keyboard, game still decided to make my controller vibrate and fall off my table.

I've seen a lot of flack for this game but while I have some gripes I've still really enjoyed it. I've so far really enjoyed the visual style of the game. The vampires look nosferatu levels of monstrous which is a nice change from modern depictions. The playable characters all seem really unique and despite playing single player I haven't found any situation I can't handle with any particular characters skill sets. Some of the old Arkane "play-your-way" stuff is even still here despite the relative size of the world to their old games (certain buildings will have multiple entry points etc.) For me at least the game performs really well on a intel i5 12600 and a RTX 2080 super on ultra setting at 2k resolution.

My issues with the game are mostly the sort of things that have been included to facilitate multiplayer. The lack of pausing and saving in single player mode for example. The customisation options for guns are a little minimal so buying a particular type of weapon isn't a guarantee of a particular characteristic (silencer). All the other issues are things I would expect to come out in the wash (buggy ai, some non-gamebreaking glitches, etc.)

Overall, I'm having fun in redfall.
